findings.title: SQL Injection in SELECT query
findings.description: User-supplied input 'term' is directly interpolated into a SQL query string, allowing SQL injection.
findings.evidence: query = f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE display_name = '{term}'"
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries (e.g., with placeholders like ? or :param) instead of string formatting.

judge.reason: No explicit judge decision was returned.

findings.title: Command Injection via shell=True and formatted string
findings.description: User-supplied input 'name' is directly interpolated into a command string executed with shell=True, allowing arbitrary command execution.
findings.evidence: subprocess.check_output(f"echo {name}", shell=True, text=True)
findings.remediation: Avoid shell=True; use subprocess.run with a list of arguments. If shell is required, sanitize input thoroughly or use shlex.quote.

judge.reason: No explicit judge decision was returned.

findings.title: Debug mode enabled in production
findings.description: The Flask application has debug mode enabled both in configuration (app.config["DEBUG"] = True) and when running (app.run(debug=True)). In production, this can expose sensitive information and allow arbitrary code execution through the Werkzeug debugger.
findings.evidence: app.py line 8: app.config["DEBUG"] = True app.py line 42: app.run(debug=True, host="127.0.0.1")
findings.remediation: Set DEBUG=False in app.config and debug=False in app.run() for production deployments. Use environment variables or configuration files to toggle debug mode only in development.

judge.reason: No explicit judge decision was returned.
